# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- luau

def luau(root):
    """The ScreenGui instance tree as a script that builds it in place.

    Same transport choice as roblox-animation's to_roblox.py, and for the same
    reason: a UI tree is dozens of instances, so execute_luau needs no Rojo
    session and no plugin, and there is no live connection to wedge.

    IT TAKES THE WHOLE ROOT, the same dict the .model.json is written from. The
    root's properties used to be hardcoded here while the .model.json path set
    `Enabled` from the page kind - installed through Rojo you got a hidden page,
    installed through execute_luau every page was Enabled at once. Later the
    CanvasFrame was missing from this path too. Emitting from the one root makes
    both impossible.

    A same-named ScreenGui already in StarterGui is replaced, so re-pasting a
    page does not stack two copies.
    """
    name = root["name"]
    lines = ["-- generated by ui_build.py; paste into execute_luau",
             "local StarterGui = game:GetService('StarterGui')",
             f"local old = StarterGui:FindFirstChild('{name}')",
             "if old then old:Destroy() end",
             ""]
    idx = [0]

    def emit(node, parent):
        idx[0] += 1
        v = f"o{idx[0]}"
        lines.append(f"local {v} = Instance.new('{node['className']}')")
        if node.get("name"):
            lines.append(f"{v}.Name = {lua_value(node['name'], prop='Name')}")
        for k, val in (node.get("properties") or {}).items():
            lines.append(f"{v}.{k} = {lua_value(val, prop=k)}")
        for k, val in (node.get("attributes") or {}).items():
            # An attribute can NEVER be an Enum - SetAttribute does not accept
            # one - so the enum guess must not run here at all.
            lines.append(f'{v}:SetAttribute("{k}", {lua_value(val, is_attribute=True)})')
        if parent:
            lines.append(f"{v}.Parent = {parent}")
        for c in node.get("children") or []:
            emit(c, v)
        return v

    top = emit(root, None)
    lines += ["", f"{top}.Parent = StarterGui",
              f"print('[ui] built {name} with', #{top}:GetDescendants(), 'descendants')"]
    return "\n".join(lines)


# Properties whose value is ALWAYS a plain string, never an enum shorthand.
# Deciding by property name is the only correct way: an all-caps label like
# "VICTORY" is indistinguishable from an enum member by shape alone, and the old
# value-shape heuristic turned it into `Enum.VICTORY`.
STRING_PROPS = {
    "Text", "Image", "Name", "PlaceholderText", "TextureID", "Texture",
    "SoundId", "Value", "Title", "ImageRectOffset", "ContentId",
}

# An enum shorthand is one or more CamelCase tokens joined by dots. BOTH forms
# occur in a spec: the bare member ("Fit", "Sibling") and the fully qualified
# path ("ApplyStrokeMode.Border", "TextXAlignment.Center"), because Enum.<v>
# produces valid Luau either way. An earlier version of this pattern allowed
# only the bare form, which sent every qualified enum down the string branch and
# made Roblox reject it at ASSIGN time with
#   Unable to assign property ApplyStrokeMode. Invalid value
#   "ApplyStrokeMode.Border" for enum ApplyStrokeMode
# - a failure that parses cleanly and only shows up when the script actually runs.
_ENUM_TOKEN = __import__("re").compile(r"^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9]+)*$")


# Content-typed properties CANNOT travel through a live Rojo session.
#
# Measured 2026-09-06, with the exact error kept because the symptom is so
# misleading: connecting a session died with
#
#   RbxDom.EncodedValue:196: unexpected Content value 'rbxassetid://1234567890'
#
# and NOTHING synced - no code, no GUI, an untouched place. `rojo build` (the
# Rust CLI) accepts the same file happily, so every offline gate passed. The
# mismatch is between the CLI's encoder and the PLUGIN's bundled Lua decoder for
# Roblox's newer Content type, and it is not fixable from the spec: tagging it as
# {"Content": "..."} fails identically, because the CLI re-encodes it either way.
#
# So the .model.json - the file Rojo serves - carries NO Content property at all.
# The icon's NAME rides along as an attribute instead, and the id is applied at
# runtime from a generated bank. The PNG mockup and the Luau builder are
# unaffected and still carry the real id.
CONTENT_PROPS = {"Image", "TextureID", "Texture", "SoundId", "MeshId", "ContentId"}


# WHICH LAYER DRAWS ON TOP. Every ScreenGui shipped at DisplayOrder 0, which
# does not mean "in spec order" - it means UNDEFINED, and Roblox is free to
# draw a modal page underneath the HUD. It did: the fighter-select scrim
# rendered BELOW the round timer, so a "NEXT ROUND / 0:06" panel sat on top of
# "CHOOSE YOUR FIGHTER" and the select screen read as broken UI rather than as
# a modal. Nothing catches this offline - the tree is correct, the mockup is
# correct (it composites in spec order), and only the engine disagrees.
#
# The order is the obvious one: the HUD is the floor, transient overlays sit
# above it, and a modal page that takes input covers everything.
DISPLAY_ORDER = {"hud": 1, "overlay": 5, "page": 10}


def strip_content_for_rojo(node):
    """Remove Content-typed properties from the tree Rojo will serve, in place."""
    if not isinstance(node, dict):
        return node
    props = node.get("properties")
    if isinstance(props, dict):
        for k in list(props):
            if k in CONTENT_PROPS:
                props.pop(k)
    for child in node.get("children") or []:
        strip_content_for_rojo(child)
    return node


def lua_value(v, prop: str | None = None, is_attribute: bool = False):
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "true" if v else "false"
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return str(v)
    if isinstance(v, str):
        # THREE REASONS A STRING IS NEVER AN ENUM, all of which shipped invalid
        # Luau before this was fixed (2026-09-05, four of five screens failed to
        # COMPILE with "Expected identifier, got ')'"):
        #   1. An EMPTY string. "" passed every clause of the old shape
        #      heuristic and emitted the bare token `Enum.`, which is a syntax
        #      error. It reached the emitter through Text="" and, ironically,
        #      through the PendingIcon="" that exists to overwrite a stale Rojo
        #      attribute - so the fix for one defect created another.
        #   2. An ATTRIBUTE. SetAttribute cannot take an Enum at all.
        #   3. A property that is always textual - see STRING_PROPS.
        if not v or is_attribute or prop in STRING_PROPS:
            return '"' + v.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
        # A bare string property is either a real string or an enum shorthand.
        if "://" in v or " " in v or not _ENUM_TOKEN.match(v):
            return '"' + v.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
        return f"Enum.{v}"
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        if "UDim2" in v:
            (sx, ox), (sy, oy) = v["UDim2"]
            return f"UDim2.new({sx}, {ox}, {sy}, {oy})"
        if "UDim" in v:
            s, o = v["UDim"]
            return f"UDim.new({s}, {o})"
        if "Color3" in v:
            r, g, b = v["Color3"]
            return f"Color3.new({r}, {g}, {b})"
        if "Vector2" in v:
            x, y = v["Vector2"]
            return f"Vector2.new({x}, {y})"
        if "ColorSequence" in v:
            kps = ", ".join(
                f"ColorSequenceKeypoint.new({k['time']}, Color3.new({k['color'][0]}, "
                f"{k['color'][1]}, {k['color'][2]}))" for k in v["ColorSequence"]["keypoints"])
            return f"ColorSequence.new({{{kps}}})"
        if "NumberSequence" in v:  # pattern fades (added with patterns.py)
            kps = ", ".join(
                f"NumberSequenceKeypoint.new({k['time']}, {k['value']}, {k.get('envelope', 0)})"
                for k in v["NumberSequence"]["keypoints"])
            return f"NumberSequence.new({{{kps}}})"
        if "Font" in v:
            return ("Font.new(\"rbxasset://fonts/families/FredokaOne.json\", "
                    "Enum.FontWeight.Regular, Enum.FontStyle.Normal)")
    return "nil"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- enum fix

ENUM_PROPS = {"ScaleType", "TextXAlignment", "ApplyStrokeMode", "LineJoinMode",
              "ZIndexBehavior", "TextYAlignment",
              "SortOrder", "FillDirection", "HorizontalAlignment",
              "VerticalAlignment", "DominantAxis"}


def qualify_enums(node):
    """Rojo takes enums as bare strings; Luau needs Enum.Prop.Value.

    Kept as a separate pass so the .model.json stays in Rojo's dialect and only
    the Luau emitter sees the qualified form.
    """
    for k, v in (node.get("properties") or {}).items():
        if k in ENUM_PROPS and isinstance(v, str) and not v.startswith("Enum."):
            node["properties"][k] = f"{k}.{v}"
    for c in node.get("children") or []:
        qualify_enums(c)
    return node


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- cli

def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("spec")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--icons", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--png", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--model", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--luau", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--icon-map", default=None,
                    help="icons.json from upload_icons.py; without it the emitted "
                         "tree carries named placeholders instead of asset ids")
    ap.add_argument("--keep-content", action="store_true",
                    help="keep Image ids in the .model.json (default strips them; "
                         "see strip_content_for_rojo for the live-sync risk)")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not (args.png or args.model or args.luau):
        args.png = args.model = args.luau = True  # no output named = build all three

    if args.icon_map and Path(args.icon_map).exists():
        ICON_IDS.update({k: v for k, v in
                         json.loads(Path(args.icon_map).read_text()).items()
                         if not k.startswith("_")})
    elif args.icon_map:
        print(f"[icons] {args.icon_map} not found; emitting empty images")

    spec_path = Path(args.spec)
    spec = json.loads(spec_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    theme = spec["theme"]
    if isinstance(theme, str):
        theme = json.loads(resolve_theme_path(spec_path.parent, theme).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    palette = theme.get("palette", {})
    set_style(theme)
    size = spec.get("resolution", [1280, 720])
    out = Path(args.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stem = spec.get("name", Path(args.spec).stem)

    icons = {}
    if args.icons:
        icons = {p.stem: p for p in Path(args.icons).glob("*.png")}

    root_spec = {"type": "root", "name": stem, "size": [1, 0, 1, 0],
                 "children": spec["children"]}

    if args.png:
        root = resolve(root_spec, (0, 0, size[0], size[1]), theme)
        img = render(root, theme, palette, icons, size)
        img.convert("RGB").save(out / f"{stem}.png")
        print(f"[png]   {out / f'{stem}.png'}  {size[0]}x{size[1]}"
              f"  {sum(1 for _ in walk(root))} nodes")

    if args.model or args.luau:
        # Measure BEFORE emitting: the emitter needs resolved pixel heights.
        measure_heights(root_spec, theme, size)
        tree = [i for c in spec["children"] for i in to_instances(c, theme, palette)]
        root = build_root(spec, stem, tree)
        # ONE ROOT, TWO TRANSPORTS, and the copy is the point. The .model.json and
        # the Luau builder used to be assembled separately: the Luau had NO
        # CanvasFrame at all (so a pasted page and a Rojo page were different
        # trees), and strip_content_for_rojo mutated the SHARED tree in place, so
        # with --model --luau together the Luau builder silently lost every icon
        # id as well. Found while building a real game.
        if args.model:
            rojo_root = copy.deepcopy(root)
            # --keep-content ships the real rbxassetid in the .model.json. `rojo
            # build` accepts it; the measured risk is the LIVE plugin (7.2.1 here),
            # which died on a Content value and synced nothing. IconName still
            # rides along, so a runtime applier works either way.
            if not args.keep_content:
                strip_content_for_rojo(rojo_root)
            # The root's name comes from the FILE name; Rojo 6+ ignores (and
            # warns on) a top-level name field, once per screen.
            rojo_root.pop("name", None)
            (out / f"{stem}.model.json").write_text(json.dumps(rojo_root, indent=2))
            print(f"[model] {out / f'{stem}.model.json'}")
        if args.luau:
            (out / f"{stem}.lua").write_text(luau(qualify_enums(copy.deepcopy(root))))
            print(f"[luau]  {out / f'{stem}.lua'}")
    return 0


def _open_attrs() -> dict:
    o = STYLE["motion"].get("open")
    if not o:
        return {}
    return {"OpenStyle": str(o.get("style", "pop")), "OpenFrom": float(o.get("from", 0.85)),
            "OpenTime": float(o.get("time", 0.16))}


def build_root(spec, stem, tree):
    """The ScreenGui instance tree both transports emit.

    The CanvasFrame convention: one full-size transparent parent so the page
    never floats on the ScreenGui and 0-1 means the screen. RESPONSIVENESS lives
    in ONE UIScale, mapping the reference resolution to the player's viewport.

    `scaleOn` says where that UIScale goes:
      "canvas" (default)  under the CanvasFrame, driven by the skill's
                          references/UIController.client.lua.
      "screen"            directly under the ScreenGui. For a game whose own
                          controller does `screen:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
                          or Instance.new("UIScale")` - shipping it on the canvas
                          there gives TWO UIScales, which multiply.

    `enabled` overrides the page-kind default (only "hud" starts Enabled), for a
    screen that must start exactly as some existing code expects.
    """
    ref = spec.get("resolution", [1280, 720])
    page_kind = spec.get("kind", "page")
    scale = instance("Scale", "UIScale", {"Scale": 1})
    on_screen = spec.get("scaleOn", "canvas") == "screen"
    canvas = instance("CanvasFrame", "Frame", {
        "Size": {"UDim2": [[1, 0], [1, 0]]},
        "Position": {"UDim2": [[0.5, 0], [0.5, 0]]},
        "AnchorPoint": {"Vector2": [0.5, 0.5]},
        "BackgroundTransparency": 1},
        ([] if on_screen else [scale]) + tree,
        attributes={"RefWidth": ref[0], "RefHeight": ref[1]})
    enabled = spec.get("enabled", page_kind == "hud")
    return instance(stem, "ScreenGui", {
        "DisplayOrder": spec.get("displayOrder",
                                 DISPLAY_ORDER.get(page_kind, DISPLAY_ORDER["page"])),
        "ResetOnSpawn": False,
        "ZIndexBehavior": "Sibling",
        "IgnoreGuiInset": bool(spec.get("ignoreGuiInset", False)),
        "Enabled": bool(enabled)},
        ([scale] if on_screen else []) + [canvas],
        # Page-level attributes pass straight through, so a spec can tell the
        # client something about the SCREEN that no element carries.
        attributes={"UIKind": page_kind, **_open_attrs(), **(spec.get("attributes") or {})})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prove every ImageLabel in a shipped UI tree will actually get a picture.

THE DEFECT THIS EXISTS FOR. On 2026-08-31 a build shipped three empty
ImageLabels in its HUD with every gate green: the icons were generated, cut out
and visible in the mockup PNG, but nobody had uploaded them, so the shipped
`.model.json` carried `Image=""` and the game rendered three blank boxes.

`verify_wired.py` checks for exactly that - an ImageLabel with no Image - by
reading the instance files. THAT CHECK IS WRONG FOR A RUNTIME-RESOLVED UI, and
this script is the right one.

Rojo refuses to serve Content-typed properties, so a UI built through Rojo
CANNOT carry `Image` in its `.model.json` at all. The working pattern is to
strip Image at build time, leave an `IconName` ATTRIBUTE on each ImageLabel, and
have a controller apply the id from a generated bank at runtime. Under that
pattern verify_wired.py reports one FAIL per icon and every one is a false
positive - while the REAL failure it should be catching (an IconName with no
entry in the bank, or an ImageLabel with no attribute at all) is invisible to it.

So this checks the mechanism that actually ships:

  every ImageLabel  ->  has an IconName attribute
  every IconName    ->  resolves to an entry in the generated icon bank
  the bank          ->  has at least one entry, and each is a real asset id

A run that finds ZERO ImageLabels or an EMPTY bank exits 2, not 0. A verifier
that cannot find its own target has failed, not passed - reporting "0 problems"
after matching nothing is how a broken check survives for months.

    python verify_icon_wiring.py --gui src/StarterGui --bank src/shared/Config/UiIcons.luau

Exit codes: 0 all wired, 1 at least one icon will render blank, 2 the check
could not find its target.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

BANK_ENTRY = re.compile(r'^\s*\[?"?(\w+)"?\]?\s*=\s*"(rbxassetid://\d+)"', re.M)


def load_bank(path: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    text = path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    return {name: asset for name, asset in BANK_ENTRY.findall(text)}


def walk(node, path: str, out: list):
    if not isinstance(node, dict):
        return
    name = node.get("name", "?")
    here = f"{path}/{name}"
    if node.get("className") == "ImageLabel":
        out.append((here, (node.get("attributes") or {}).get("IconName")))
    for child in node.get("children") or []:
        walk(child, here, out)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
    )
    ap.add_argument("--gui", required=True, type=pathlib.Path, help="directory of *.model.json instance files")
    ap.add_argument("--bank", required=True, type=pathlib.Path, help="the generated icon bank Luau module")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if not args.bank.exists():
        print(f"FAIL: icon bank not found at {args.bank}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    bank = load_bank(args.bank)

    labels: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []
    files = sorted(args.gui.glob("*.model.json"))
    for f in files:
        walk(json.loads(f.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")), f.stem, labels)

    missing = [p for p, icon in labels if not icon]
    unresolved = [(p, icon) for p, icon in labels if icon and icon not in bank]
    wired = len(labels) - len(missing) - len(unresolved)

    print(f"icon bank  : {len(bank)} entries ({', '.join(sorted(bank))})")
    print(f"gui files  : {len(files)}")
    print(f"ImageLabels: {len(labels)}   wired {wired}   no attribute {len(missing)}   unresolved {len(unresolved)}")
    for p in missing:
        print(f"  FAIL {p}: no IconName attribute - it will render blank")
    for p, icon in unresolved:
        print(f"  FAIL {p}: IconName '{icon}' has no entry in the bank - it will render blank")

    if not files or not labels or not bank:
        print(
            "\nFAIL: this check matched nothing (no files, no ImageLabels, or an empty bank).\n"
            "That is a failure, not a pass - a verifier must find its own target.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    if missing or unresolved:
        return 1

    print("\nevery ImageLabel resolves to an uploaded icon")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Every dynamic label in the shipped UI must be written by some controller.

    python verify_labels.py --ui src/ui --client src/client

THE DEFECT THIS EXISTS FOR, measured 2026-09-09. The HUD shipped with four
labels that no line of code anywhere could ever write: AmmoCounter had no remote
at all (ammo lived in a server-side table nobody broadcast), and the freezing
panel had three rows fed by a roster that did not carry a frozen flag. They sat
on screen for an entire run rendering their mockup placeholder.

Nothing caught it, and that is the interesting part. `rojo build` passed. 53
specs passed. selene and stylua passed. `verify_ui.py` passed, because it checks
LAYOUT - nothing touching, nothing off-centre - and a dead label is laid out
perfectly. The PNG mockup agreed with the game because both are drawn from the
same tree. Every gate was measuring internal consistency, and a placeholder is
perfectly internally consistent.

So this asks the one question none of them did: for each label carrying the
placeholder, does any client controller mention its name?

It is a static check and it can be fooled by a controller that mentions a name
without writing it. That is fine - it costs nothing and it catches the failure
that actually happened, which is a label with NO reference anywhere at all.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                             formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
ap.add_argument("--ui", default="src/ui", help="directory of built *.model.json screens")
ap.add_argument("--client", default="src/client", help="client source tree that must bind them")
ap.add_argument("--sentinel", default="<unbound>",
                help="the placeholder string. It MUST be one the live code can never produce - "
                     "'--' reads as a plausible empty value, which is how four dead labels shipped")
_a = ap.parse_args()
UI_DIR = pathlib.Path(_a.ui)
CLIENT_DIR = pathlib.Path(_a.client)

# The placeholder is deliberately a string the live code can never produce. It
# used to be "--", which reads as a plausible empty value - which is exactly why
# four dead labels looked like "nothing yet" rather than like a bug.
SENTINEL = _a.sentinel


def is_referenced(name: str, src: str) -> bool:
    """Does any controller name this label?

    Two shapes, and the second one is why this function exists rather than a
    single `in` test. A controller may name a label OUTRIGHT ("AmmoCount"), or
    ASSEMBLE it from a row index - `BankRow{i}` .. "Name" - in which case the
    string "BankRow1Name" appears nowhere in the source at all.

    A first version of this check only understood the literal form and reported
    ten working labels as dead. The settlement screen had been seen in game
    listing real sheep names, so the check was wrong, not the code - and a gate
    that cries wolf gets switched off, which is worse than not having it.

    So: split the name on digit runs and require every remaining segment. That
    is weaker for a name whose segments are common words, and it is exact for
    the failure that actually happened - a label mentioned NOWHERE.
    """
    if f'"{name}"' in src:
        return True
    if not re.search(r"\d", name):
        # No index in the name, so there is nothing to assemble it from: the
        # literal is the only way it can be written, and it was not. This is
        # the branch that catches a genuinely dead label.
        return False
    # An indexed name: FrozenRow1 is written as `FrozenRow{i}`, BankRow1Name as
    # `BankRow{i}` .. "Name". Require every non-digit segment.
    return all(seg in src for seg in re.split(r"\d+", name) if seg)


# A label with a GENERIC name is written through its parent: UiController-style
# SetText(screen, "CashLabel", ...) lands in CashLabel's child called "Text".
# Checking the literal "Text" passed trivially - every controller mentions it -
# so a dead Text child under a parent nobody names would sail through. The name
# that must be referenced is the nearest ancestor that is not generic.
GENERIC = {"Text", "Label", "Caption", "Value", "Face", "Title"}


def labels_with_placeholder(node, out, path="", owner=""):
    """Every named node whose Text is the sentinel, with the name that binds it."""
    name = node.get("name", "")
    props = node.get("properties", {}) or {}
    binder = owner if name in GENERIC else name
    if props.get("Text") == SENTINEL and name:
        out.append((binder or name, path + "/" + name))
    for child in node.get("children", []) or []:
        labels_with_placeholder(child, out, path + "/" + name,
                                binder if name and not name.endswith("Cell") else owner)
    return out


def main() -> int:
    if not UI_DIR.is_dir():
        print(f"FAIL: no {UI_DIR}")
        return 1

    client_src = "\n".join(
        p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        for p in CLIENT_DIR.rglob("*.luau")
    )

    problems = []
    checked = 0
    for model in sorted(UI_DIR.glob("*.model.json")):
        tree = json.loads(model.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for name, path in labels_with_placeholder(tree, []):
            checked += 1
            if not is_referenced(name, client_src):
                problems.append(f"{model.name}{path}  (name '{name}' appears in NO controller)")

    if checked == 0:
        print("FAIL: no label carries the sentinel - this check matched nothing, "
              "which is a failure, not a pass")
        return 2
    if problems:
        print(f"FAIL: {len(problems)} of {checked} dynamic labels are written by nothing:")
        for p in problems:
            print("  " + p)
        print()
        print("A label nobody writes renders its placeholder for the whole run.")
        return 1

    print(f"PASS: all {checked} dynamic labels are referenced by a controller")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Static checks on a UI spec, before anything renders.

    python verify_ui.py specs/*.json [--strict]

WHY STATIC AND NOT A SCREENSHOT. A screenshot answers "does this look right at
1280x720", which is the question you can already answer by eye. These checks
answer the questions a render CANNOT: what happens on a phone, what happens under
the player's thumb, and whether a construction is one Roblox silently refuses to
draw. Every one of them has a recorded failure behind it.

THE CHECKS

  offset_size      Size or Position in OFFSET where scale was meant. The number
                   one cause of broken mobile UI, and it looks perfect on the
                   machine it was authored on. Offset is legitimate for a fixed
                   gutter, so this reports rather than fails unless --strict.
  touch_target     Any button under 44pt on the WORST supported device, measured
                   at the reference resolution times that device's UIScale. This
                   is the check that stops "add a UIScale" being mistaken for a
                   mobile strategy: uniform downscaling takes a 68px button to
                   39pt on a handset, and 39pt is a missed tap.
  viewport_fit     The scaled page does not fit the device at all.
  safe_zone        Anything inside the thumbstick zone, the jump zone, or the
                   36px Roblox top bar inset. Skipped inside a "modal": true
                   window, because those controls are not drawn while a dialog
                   is up.
  rotated_clip     A rotated element inside a ClipsDescendants parent. Roblox
                   DOES NOT CLIP ROTATED DESCENDANTS: it lints clean, exits 0,
                   and throws diagonal bands across the viewport.
  stroke_mix       More than one outer stroke thickness on one page. Mixed stroke
                   weight is the clearest tell of beginner or generated UI.
  grid_aspect      A UIGridLayout with no UIAspectRatioConstraint on its cells.
  missing_icon     An icon the icon folder does not contain, which renders as
                   nothing at all rather than as an error.
  text_fit         A label whose text does not fit its box at the designed size.
                   Roblox's TextScaled does NOT overflow - it SHRINKS, without
                   limit, so the real symptom is not text outside a frame but text
                   that has quietly become unreadable. This measures the shrink
                   with the real font and fails when the on-device result drops
                   below a legible size.
  overflow         A child whose resolved rect leaves its parent. Set
                   "overhang": true on an element that is MEANT to sit proud of
                   its parent, such as a close button on a window corner - a
                   check that cries wolf stops being read.

A check that cannot fail is not a check. `--self-test` sabotages a spec in each
of these ways and asserts every one goes red.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import copy
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import ui_build  # noqa: E402
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw  # noqa: E402

# One throwaway canvas to measure text against. Measuring needs a draw context and
# the real font, which is the whole point: a width check done with an assumed
# character width is a guess, and Fredoka is much wider than most.
_measure_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(Image.new("RGB", (8, 8)))

# Real viewports, not round numbers. These are what the checks are evaluated at,
# because "does it work on mobile" is not answerable at one size.
DEVICES = [
    ("phone-small", 640, 360),      # the floor worth supporting, landscape
    ("phone", 896, 414),            # a modern handset, landscape
    ("tablet", 1024, 768),
    ("desktop", 1920, 1080),
]
SMALL = (640, 360)
TOUCH_MIN = 44
TOPBAR = 36

# The pages are authored at a reference resolution in OFFSET and mapped to the
# viewport by ONE UIScale on the CanvasFrame - see ui_build.py. These bounds must
# match UIController.client.lua exactly or the checker is measuring a UI that does
# not ship.
#
# The cap exists because uncapped scaling makes a 1440p screen's UI enormous.
#
# THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO FLOOR. A floor was tried at 0.60 and it was the wrong
# lever: it made the page render at 768x432 on a 640x360 phone, so it no longer
# FIT, which is worse than being small. Touch targets are protected by making the
# base controls big enough at the reference resolution instead - which is what
# "mobile first" actually costs - and the touch_target check below is what says by
# how much.
SCALE_MIN, SCALE_MAX = 0.0, 1.25

# Smallest text worth shipping, in points on the WORST supported device. Below
# this a label is present but not readable, which is the failure TextScaled hides
# by shrinking instead of overflowing.
MIN_TEXT_PT = 11
# A label forced below this fraction of its designed size is a layout problem even
# if it is still legible - the design asked for a size the box cannot give.
MIN_TEXT_RATIO = 0.55


def ui_scale(vw: int, vh: int, ref_w: int, ref_h: int) -> float:
    return max(SCALE_MIN, min(SCALE_MAX, min(vw / ref_w, vh / ref_h)))
# Fractions of the screen, from mobile control-zone measurements. The thumbstick sits bottom-left and
# the jump button bottom-right, and both are drawn by Roblox over your UI.
THUMBSTICK = (0.0, 0.62, 0.30, 1.0)
JUMPZONE = (0.76, 0.68, 1.0, 1.0)
# Roblox draws its own PLAYER LIST in the top-right corner of every experience
# unless the game turns it off. This checker did not know that, so a combo
# counter pinned to the top-right corner passed every zone check and was then
# completely hidden behind the roster the moment a second player joined - a
# defect that is INVISIBLE in a solo playtest and in every mockup, because
# neither draws the CoreGui. Roughly 260x220 at a 1280x720 reference, and it
# grows with longer usernames, so the zone is generous on purpose.
PLAYERLIST = (0.79, 0.0, 1.0, 0.31)


# --------------------------------------------------------------- layout hygiene
#
# THREE THINGS A HUMAN NOTICES IMMEDIATELY AND NO EXISTING CHECK COULD SEE.
# Every one of them was reported by eye on a build where this checker said the
# page was clean, which is the definition of a missing check.
#
# MIN_GAP_PX  Sibling elements must not touch. Two controls with zero space
#             between them read as one control with a line through it, and at
#             the smallest supported scale a 1px gap is 0px. Measured at the
#             REFERENCE resolution, so it survives scaling.
# CENTRE_TOL  "Centred" is not a property, it is a measurement: the rendered
#             centre against the parent's centre. The classic Roblox bug is a
#             0.5 scale position with no 0.5 anchor, which lands the element
#             half its own size off centre and looks almost right.
# WRAP_TIGHT  A container drawn tight around a single child reads as a BOX
#             around it - the box-behind-the-button defect. A frame
#             that exists only to position something must be transparent.
MIN_GAP_PX = 8
CENTRE_TOL_PX = 1.5
WRAP_TIGHT_PX = 6


def rects(spec, theme, size):
    root = {"type": "root", "size": [1, 0, 1, 0], "children": spec["children"]}
    node = ui_build.resolve(root, (0, 0, size[0], size[1]), theme)
    return node


def overlaps(rect, zone, size):
    x, y, w, h = rect
    zx0, zy0, zx1, zy1 = (zone[0] * size[0], zone[1] * size[1],
                          zone[2] * size[0], zone[3] * size[1])
    return not (x + w <= zx0 or x >= zx1 or y + h <= zy0 or y >= zy1)


def check(spec, theme, icons, path):
    issues = []

    def add(level, code, msg):
        issues.append({"level": level, "check": code, "where": path, "msg": msg})

    ref = spec.get("resolution", [1280, 720])
    big = rects(spec, theme, ref)
    small = rects(spec, theme, SMALL)

    # Every device the design claims to support, and the worst case across them.
    scales = {name: ui_scale(vw, vh, ref[0], ref[1]) for name, vw, vh in DEVICES}
    worst_dev, worst_scale = min(scales.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])

    for name, vw, vh in DEVICES:
        sc = scales[name]
        page_w, page_h = ref[0] * sc, ref[1] * sc
        if page_w > vw + 1 or page_h > vh + 1:
            add("fail", "viewport_fit",
                f"at {name} {vw}x{vh} the page scales to {page_w:.0f}x{page_h:.0f} "
                f"and does not fit; the UIScale floor of {SCALE_MIN} is too high "
                f"for this reference resolution")

    strokes = set()

    def visit(node, parent_spec, small_node, in_modal=False):
        s = node.spec
        in_modal = in_modal or bool(s.get("modal"))
        kind = s.get("type", "frame")
        name = s.get("name") or kind

        sz, po = s.get("size", [1, 0, 1, 0]), s.get("pos", [0, 0, 0, 0])
        if kind in ("panel", "button", "frame") and s.get("children"):
            if sz[0] == 0 and sz[2] == 0 and sz[1] and sz[3]:
                add("info", "offset_size",
                    f"{name} is sized purely in offset ({sz[1]}x{sz[3]}); it will not "
                    "scale with the screen")

        # TEXT FIT. Measured for a label AND for a button's own caption (a caption
        # written as a button's "text" used to be skipped, so it could shrink to a
        # smear unchecked), and for every declared SAMPLE as well as the text.
        #
        # SAMPLES exist because of the sentinel rule: a dynamic label ships as
        # "<unbound>", nine characters, so measuring only the shipped text proves
        # nothing about "Wasps fly! Only Soda Cannons, Bug Zappers and the
        # Magnifying Glass hit them". "samples": [...] lists the longest strings
        # the live code will actually write; they are measured, never shipped.
        texts = []
        # The sentinel itself is never what the player reads, so it is not measured:
        # declare "samples" for a dynamic label instead (the sentinel gate still runs).
        if kind in ("label", "button") and str(s.get("text", "")) and s.get("text") != "<unbound>":
            texts.append(str(s["text"]))
        if kind in ("label", "button"):
            texts += [str(t) for t in s.get("samples") or []]
        for txt in texts:
            _, _, rw, rh = node.rect
            designed = int(rh * s.get("textScale", 0.62))
            if designed < 6 or rw <= 0:
                continue
            stroke = int(s.get("textStroke", theme["textStroke"]))
            fitted = ui_build.fit_text_size(_measure_draw, txt, designed, (rw, rh),
                                            stroke, wrap=bool(s.get("wrap")))
            on_device = fitted * worst_scale
            if fitted < designed * MIN_TEXT_RATIO:
                add("fail", "text_fit",
                    f"{name}: {txt!r} only fits at {fitted}px in a "
                    f"{rw:.0f}x{rh:.0f} box, down from the designed {designed}px "
                    f"({fitted / designed:.0%}). Widen the box or shorten the text.")
            elif on_device < MIN_TEXT_PT:
                add("fail", "text_fit",
                    f"{name}: {txt!r} renders at {on_device:.0f}pt on "
                    f"{worst_dev} - under the {MIN_TEXT_PT}pt legibility floor.")

        if kind == "button":
            # Measure at the REFERENCE size and apply the UIScale, which is how the
            # element actually gets to the device. Resolving the tree at 640x360
            # instead would model a page that reflows, and this one does not.
            _, _, rw, rh = node.rect
            eff = min(rw, rh) * worst_scale
            if eff < TOUCH_MIN:
                add("fail", "touch_target",
                    f"{name} is {min(rw, rh):.0f}px at the {ref[0]}x{ref[1]} "
                    f"reference, which is {eff:.0f}pt on {worst_dev} "
                    f"(scale {worst_scale:.2f}) - under the {TOUCH_MIN}pt minimum. "
                    f"It needs to be at least {TOUCH_MIN / worst_scale:.0f}px.")
            # The thumbstick and jump button only exist while the player is
            # DRIVING. A modal window is on top and movement is not the task, so
            # the zones apply to HUD-style overlay elements, not to dialogs.
            # Without this the check fires on the bottom-right control of every
            # centred window, which is most of them, and stops being read.
            if not in_modal:
                # Map the REFERENCE rect onto the device the same way the UIScale
                # does: scale it, then centre the scaled page in the viewport.
                # Re-resolving the tree at the device size instead would model a
                # page that reflows, and this one does not - which is why the
                # sabotage test stopped tripping when touch_target moved to the
                # scale model and this did not.
                for dev, vw, vh in DEVICES:
                    sc = scales[dev]
                    ox = (vw - ref[0] * sc) / 2
                    oy = (vh - ref[1] * sc) / 2
                    rx, ry, rw, rh = node.rect
                    dev_rect = (ox + rx * sc, oy + ry * sc, rw * sc, rh * sc)
                    for zone, label in ((THUMBSTICK, "thumbstick"),
                                        (JUMPZONE, "jump button"),
                                        (PLAYERLIST, "Roblox player list")):
                        if overlaps(dev_rect, zone, (vw, vh)):
                            add("fail", "safe_zone",
                                f"{name} sits in the {label} zone on {dev} "
                                f"({vw}x{vh})")
                            break
                    else:
                        continue
                    break
            if not in_modal and small_node.rect[1] < TOPBAR:
                add("warn", "safe_zone",
                    f"{name} runs into the {TOPBAR}px Roblox top bar inset")

        if s.get("rotation") and parent_spec and parent_spec.get("clips"):
            add("fail", "rotated_clip",
                f"{name} is rotated inside a ClipsDescendants parent. Roblox does not "
                "clip rotated descendants; use a UIGradient hard step instead")

        if kind in ("panel", "button") or (kind == "frame" and s.get("outline", True)
                                           and s.get("colour")):
            strokes.add(s.get("stroke", theme["stroke"]))

        lay = s.get("layout")
        if lay and lay.get("type") == "grid":
            kids = s.get("children") or []
            if kids and not any(k.get("aspect") for k in kids):
                add("warn", "grid_aspect",
                    f"{name} is a grid whose cells carry no aspect constraint; tiles "
                    "distort on a different screen ratio")

        if kind == "icon" and icons is not None and s["icon"] not in icons:
            add("fail", "missing_icon",
                f"icon '{s['icon']}' is not in the icon folder; it renders as nothing")

        if parent_spec is not None and not s.get("overhang"):
            px, py, pw, ph = node_parent_rect[id(node)]
            x, y, w, h = node.rect
            if x < px - 1 or y < py - 1 or x + w > px + pw + 1 or y + h > py + ph + 1:
                add("warn", "overflow",
                    f"{name} leaves its parent by "
                    f"{max(px - x, py - y, x + w - px - pw, y + h - py - ph):.0f}px")


        # --- SIBLINGS MUST NOT TOUCH OR OVERLAP -----------------------------
        # Overlap is a defect; a gap under MIN_GAP_PX is a defect that looks
        # like a design choice until someone sees it on a phone. Elements that
        # deliberately sit on top of things opt out with "overhang" or "modal".
        kids = [
            k for k in node.children
            if not k.spec.get("overhang") and not k.spec.get("modal")
        ]
        for i, a in enumerate(kids):
            ax0, ay0, aw, ah = a.rect
            for b in kids[i + 1:]:
                bx0, by0, bw, bh = b.rect
                ox = min(ax0 + aw, bx0 + bw) - max(ax0, bx0)
                oy = min(ay0 + ah, by0 + bh) - max(ay0, by0)
                an = a.spec.get("name") or a.spec.get("type", "element")
                bn = b.spec.get("name") or b.spec.get("type", "element")
                if ox > 0 and oy > 0:
                    add("fail", "sibling_overlap",
                        f"{an} and {bn} overlap by {min(ox, oy):.0f}px inside "
                        f"{name}; mark one 'overhang' if that is intended")
                elif ox > -MIN_GAP_PX and oy > -MIN_GAP_PX:
                    gap = max(-ox, -oy)
                    add("warn", "sibling_gap",
                        f"{an} and {bn} are {gap:.0f}px apart inside {name} "
                        f"(minimum {MIN_GAP_PX}px); elements should never touch")

        # --- CENTRED MEANS MEASURED CENTRED ---------------------------------
        # Checked on anything asking to be centred on an axis, either by saying
        # so or by sitting at 0.5 scale.
        for axis, idx, anchor_i in (("horizontally", 0, 0), ("vertically", 2, 1)):
            # "centre": false is the written-down opt-out for an element placed
            # at 0.5 scale PLUS a deliberate offset (a hotbar nudged clear of the
            # thumbstick zone). Like "overhang", it turns "off centre" into a
            # decision somebody recorded rather than a silenced check.
            if s.get("centre") is False:
                continue
            wants = s.get("centre") or s.get("centred") or (
                po[idx] == 0.5 and s.get("size", [1, 0, 1, 0])[idx] != 1
            )
            if not wants or parent_spec is None:
                continue
            px_, py_, pw_, ph_ = node_parent_rect[id(node)]
            x, y, w, h = node.rect
            mine = (x + w / 2) if idx == 0 else (y + h / 2)
            theirs = (px_ + pw_ / 2) if idx == 0 else (py_ + ph_ / 2)
            if abs(mine - theirs) > CENTRE_TOL_PX:
                off = mine - theirs
                hint = ""
                if abs(abs(off) - (w if idx == 0 else h) / 2) < 2:
                    hint = (" - that is exactly half its own size, which is a "
                            "0.5 position with no 0.5 anchor")
                add("fail", "off_centre",
                    f"{name} asks to be centred {axis} but its centre is "
                    f"{off:+.0f}px from its parent's{hint}")

        # --- NO BOX DRAWN ROUND A CONTROL -----------------------------------
        # A visible container hugging one child is not a container, it is an
        # outline the designer did not ask for.
        if (
            len(node.children) == 1
            and not s.get("transparent")
            and s.get("colour")
            and not s.get("text")
            and not s.get("icon")
            and kind in ("frame", "panel")
        ):
            cx, cy, cw, ch = node.children[0].rect
            x, y, w, h = node.rect
            pad = min(cx - x, cy - y, x + w - cx - cw, y + h - cy - ch)
            # A LABEL FILLING A COLOURED PANEL IS A CHIP, NOT A WRAPPER.
            # Narrowed 2026-09-09. The two cases this check was written for are
            # a box drawn round a BUTTON and a bar's track hugging its FILL, and
            # both still fire. Text sitting on a coloured surface is neither: it
            # is how every chip, badge, pill and header bar is built, and the
            # tell was that ui_kit's OWN window() header tripped its own check.
            # It fired ~30 times across three real pages, every one of them
            # a legitimate chip, and a gate that cries wolf gets switched off.
            # Insetting the label is not the fix either: pad is a min() over all
            # four sides, so silencing it means shrinking the label box, which
            # pushes the rendered text back under the text_fit floor. The two
            # rules only look contradictory because this one was too broad.
            if node.children[0].spec.get("type") == "label":
                pad = None
            if pad is not None and -1 <= pad <= WRAP_TIGHT_PX:
                child = node.children[0].spec
                add("warn", "wrapper_box",
                    f"{name} is an opaque frame {pad:.0f}px around "
                    f"{child.get('name') or child.get('type', 'its child')}, so it "
                    f"draws a box around it; a frame that only positions "
                    f"something needs \"transparent\": true")

        for c, sc in zip(node.children, small_node.children):
            node_parent_rect[id(c)] = node.rect
            visit(c, s, sc, in_modal)

    node_parent_rect = {}
    for c, sc in zip(big.children, small.children):
        node_parent_rect[id(c)] = big.rect
        # A TOP-LEVEL element has no parent spec, so the overflow check below
        # skipped it - which let a 726px-tall window sit on a 720px reference and
        # get clipped at both ends with nothing reported. The screen edge is a
        # parent like any other.
        x, y, w, h = c.rect
        if w > ref[0] + 1 or h > ref[1] + 1:
            add("fail", "overflow",
                f"{c.spec.get('name', 'element')} is {w:.0f}x{h:.0f}, larger than "
                f"the {ref[0]}x{ref[1]} reference screen, so it is clipped")
        visit(c, None, sc)

    if len(strokes) > 1:
        add("warn", "stroke_mix",
            f"{len(strokes)} different stroke thicknesses on one page: "
            f"{sorted(strokes)}")
    return issues


def load(path: Path):
    spec = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if "theme" not in spec or "children" not in spec:
        # specs/*.json also matches theme.json, which is not a page. Skipping it is
        # friendlier than a KeyError traceback that looks like a broken spec.
        return None, None
    theme = spec["theme"]
    if isinstance(theme, str):
        theme = json.loads(ui_build.resolve_theme_path(path.parent, theme).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return spec, theme


def run(paths, icons, strict):
    total = []
    for p in paths:
        spec, theme = load(p)
        if spec is None:
            continue
        issues = check(spec, theme, icons, p.name)
        total += issues
        fails = [i for i in issues if i["level"] == "fail"]
        print(f"\n{p.name}: {len(fails)} fail, "
              f"{sum(1 for i in issues if i['level'] == 'warn')} warn, "
              f"{sum(1 for i in issues if i['level'] == 'info')} info")
        for i in issues:
            if i["level"] != "info" or strict:
                print(f"  [{i['level']:<4}] {i['check']:<14} {i['msg']}")
    return total


def self_test(base: Path, icons) -> int:
    """Prove each check can go red. A verifier nobody has seen fail is a decoration."""
    spec, theme = load(base)
    cases = {}

    def sab(fn):
        s = copy.deepcopy(spec)
        fn(s)
        return s

    def first(s, kind):
        out = []

        def w(n):
            if n.get("type") == kind:
                out.append(n)
            for c in n.get("children") or []:
                w(c)
        for c in s["children"]:
            w(c)
        return out[0] if out else None

    # A spec need not contain a button at all - a cast HUD can be three
    # `panel`s driven by gamepad face buttons, and on that spec this sabotage
    # crashed with a TypeError on None, taking the WHOLE self-test down before a
    # single check had been proven. A self-test that cannot run is worth less
    # than no self-test, because it reads as "checked". Sabotage a button the
    # spec actually has, and otherwise plant one.
    def shrink(s):
        b = first(s, "button")
        if b is None:
            b = {"type": "button", "name": "SelfTestTarget", "colour": "red",
                 "pos": [0.5, 0, 0.5, 0], "anchor": [0.5, 0.5]}
            s["children"].append(b)
        b["size"] = [0, 20, 0, 20]
    cases["touch_target"] = sab(shrink)

    def zone(s):
        # A NEW top-level button. Moving an existing one does not work: the first
        # button in the HUD lives inside a UIListLayout, which overrides child
        # positions, so the sabotage was silently undone and the test passed by
        # accident for a while.
        s["children"].append({"type": "button", "name": "Thumbstick",
                              "colour": "red", "size": [0, 120, 0, 120],
                              "pos": [0, 10, 1, -10], "anchor": [0, 1]})
    cases["safe_zone"] = sab(zone)

    def rot(s):
        s["children"].append({"type": "panel", "name": "Chevron", "clips": True,
                              "size": [0, 200, 0, 80], "pos": [0, 20, 0, 200],
                              "children": [{"type": "frame", "name": "Slant",
                                            "colour": "gold", "rotation": 20,
                                            "size": [1, 0, 1, 0]}]})
    cases["rotated_clip"] = sab(rot)

    def strokes(s):
        # A SECOND panel at an odd thickness: re-stroking the only panel a small
        # spec has leaves one thickness on the page, which is not a mix.
        p = first(s, "panel")
        if p is not None:
            p["stroke"] = 11
        s["children"].append({"type": "panel", "name": "OtherStroke", "colour": "panel",
                              "stroke": 3, "size": [0, 120, 0, 60], "pos": [0, 600, 0, 100]})
    cases["stroke_mix"] = sab(strokes)

    # wrapper_box had NO self-test case at all until 2026-09-09, which is how it
    # went unnoticed that it was firing on every coloured chip in a page. The
    # sabotage is the exact complaint it exists for: an opaque frame hugging a
    # BUTTON. A label child is deliberately not caught any more, so sabotaging
    # with a label would now pass and prove nothing.
    def wrapped_button(s):
        s["children"].append({
            "type": "frame", "name": "AccidentalWrapper", "colour": "gold",
            "size": [0, 140, 0, 100], "pos": [0, 400, 0, 300],
            "children": [{"type": "button", "name": "Trapped", "colour": "red",
                          "size": [1, 0, 1, 0]}]})
    cases["wrapper_box"] = sab(wrapped_button)

    def squeeze(s):
        # A long string in a box built for a short one. TextScaled would shrink it
        # to a smear rather than overflow, which is exactly what must be caught.
        s["children"].append({"type": "panel", "name": "Cramped", "colour": "panel",
                              "size": [0, 90, 0, 40], "pos": [0, 300, 0, 300],
                              "children": [{"type": "label", "textScale": 0.7,
                                            "text": "a very long line of text that "
                                                    "cannot possibly fit in here",
                                            "size": [1, 0, 1, 0]}]})
    cases["text_fit"] = sab(squeeze)

    def ghost(s):
        s["children"].append({"type": "icon", "icon": "definitely_not_an_icon",
                              "size": [0, 40, 0, 40], "pos": [0, 400, 0, 400]})
    cases["missing_icon"] = sab(ghost)

    def spill(s):
        p = first(s, "panel")
        (p.setdefault("children", [])).append(
            {"type": "frame", "name": "Spill", "colour": "red",
             "size": [1, 400, 1, 0]})
    cases["overflow"] = sab(spill)

    bad = 0
    for code, s in cases.items():
        # With no --icons folder, prove missing_icon against an empty icon set.
        use = icons if (icons is not None or code != "missing_icon") else set()
        found = {i["check"] for i in check(s, theme, use, f"sabotage:{code}")}
        ok = code in found
        print(f"  {'PASS' if ok else 'MISS'}  {code:<14} "
              f"{'' if ok else 'sabotage did not trip the check'}")
        bad += 0 if ok else 1

    clean = {i["check"] for i in check(spec, theme, icons, "clean")
             if i["level"] == "fail"}
    print(f"  {'PASS' if not clean else 'MISS'}  {'baseline':<14} "
          f"{'' if not clean else f'clean spec failed: {clean}'}")
    return bad + (1 if clean else 0)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("specs", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--icons", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    paths = [Path(p) for p in args.specs]
    icons = None
    if args.icons:
        icons = {p.stem for p in Path(args.icons).glob("*.png")}

    if args.self_test:
        print("self-test: each check must go red on a sabotaged copy")
        bad = self_test(paths[0], icons)
        print(f"\n{'self-test PASSED' if not bad else f'self-test FAILED ({bad})'}")
        return 1 if bad else 0

    issues = run(paths, icons, args.strict)
    fails = sum(1 for i in issues if i["level"] == "fail")
    print(f"\n{len(paths)} specs, {fails} failures")
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

## Quick start: your first HUD in one minute

`examples/coin_hud.json` is a complete, passing spec (a coin counter, top-left).
Copy it next to your game, change it, and build:

```bash
python scripts/ui_build.py examples/coin_hud.json --out build    # PNG + .model.json + Luau
python scripts/verify_ui.py examples/coin_hud.json               # layout, text fit, touch sizes
```

- `"theme": "default"` uses `references/theme.json`. To restyle, copy that file
  next to your spec, edit it, and set `"theme": "mytheme.json"` (see Themes below).
- A label your code fills in at runtime ships as `"<unbound>"` and lists its
  longest real values in `"samples"`, which is what the text-fit check measures.
- Icons need an icons folder passed with `--icons`; leave them out until you have one.

Two halves that meet in the middle: **procedural structure** (about 80% of what
reads as modern Roblox UI needs no image at all) and a **generated icon set** for
the part that does.

Design numbers live in `references/ui-recipes.md`, measured from Roblox staff
posts and four community guides. Read it before inventing a value.

---

## The one idea this skill is built on

**A mockup drawn in a design tool is a picture of a UI, and it drifts.** So there
is no design tool here. One JSON spec resolves to one tree, and that tree emits:

| Output | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `Page.png` | The fast local probe. Sub-second, no Studio, no plugin. |
| `Page.model.json` | The deliverable. Drops into a Rojo project. |
| `Page.lua` | The transport. Paste into `execute_luau`, no Rojo session needed. |

The PNG cannot disagree with the `.model.json` about a size, a colour or a
layout, because neither is authored: both are rendered from the same resolved
tree. The Studio screenshot stays ground truth for what the renderer
approximates (font metrics, gradient banding).

This is the UI stage's version of the 2D concept gate in `roblox-3d-model`: put
the checkpoint where judging is cheap and reliable. UI is the only stage that is
natively 2D, so what you screenshot is what ships.

---

## A PLACEHOLDER MUST BE A STRING THE LIVE CODE CAN NEVER PRODUCE

**Never use `--`, `0`, `...`, `—` or an empty string as a dynamic label's
placeholder. Use a sentinel like `<unbound>`.** And then gate on it: every label
carrying the sentinel must be named by some controller, or the build fails.

Measured in a real build. A shipped HUD had four labels - an ammo counter and three
rows of a freezing panel - that **no line of code anywhere could write**. The
ammo count lived in a server-side table that was never broadcast; the freezing
rows were fed from a roster that did not carry a frozen flag. They rendered `--`
for entire runs, in front of the user, while sheep actually froze to death.

Nothing caught it, and the reason is the interesting part:

- `verify_ui.py` passed, because it checks **layout** - nothing touching, nothing
  off-centre, no box round a button. A dead label is laid out perfectly.
- The PNG mockup agreed with the game, because **both are drawn from the same
  tree**. That agreement is this skill's core strength and it is exactly why it
  cannot see this class of bug.
- `--` **reads as a plausible empty value.** It looks like "no ammo yet", not
  like "this label is wired to nothing". A sentinel that no formatter could ever
  emit turns a silent defect into an obvious one on the first screenshot.

The gate is about twenty lines: walk the built `.model.json`, collect every named
node whose `Text` is the sentinel, and require the name to appear in the client
source. Two shapes count as a reference - the literal (`"AmmoCount"`) and an
**assembled** one (`` `BankRow{i}` .. "Name" ``), so split the name on digit runs
and require each segment; a name with no digits must appear literally. Getting
that wrong matters: a first version understood only the literal form and reported
ten *working* labels as dead. **A gate that cries wolf gets switched off, which
is worse than not having one** - so when a new check disagrees with something you
have seen working in game, the check is wrong until proven otherwise.

Then prove the gate fails. Rename one binding, watch it go red, put it back. A
check that cannot fail is not a check.

## Read this first: seven things that will bite

**1. CLIP takes 77 tokens and truncates the rest SILENTLY.** The first icon batch
sent 161. Every isolation clause - "single object", "plain grey background", "no
text" - was cut before the model saw it, and four prompts came back as scenes and
pattern wallpaper. One warning line in a log was the only sign. `kaggle_run.py` (in `roblox-3d-model`)
now refuses to push an over-budget prompt, and the framing that decides usability
goes in the prompt HEAD, ahead of the subject.

**2. The Kaggle client RETURNS errors, it does not raise them.**
`dataset_create_new` on an existing dataset returns `status="error"` and the old
code caught only exceptions, so the fallback to `dataset_create_version` never
ran and the dataset sat on version 1 forever. Every reroll silently regenerated
the FIRST batch's prompts, on time, looking plausible. Prompts now carry a
`batch_id`, the kernel echoes it, and `fetch` refuses a mismatch.

**3. `ClipsDescendants` does not clip ROTATED descendants.** The angled chevron
header in every second Roblox UI reference is this trap. It lints clean, exits 0,
and throws diagonal bands across the viewport. Use a `UIGradient` hard
transparency step instead. Construction: draw the
angle as a gradient on the unrotated element, never as a rotated child inside a
clipping parent.

**4. Do not chroma key a generated icon.** Keyers compare Cb/Cr and magenta
shares the Cr axis with red, so a magenta key eats the reds and pinks that fill
an icon set. Generate on flat grey and flood fill from the border instead: this
style has a thick opaque outline, so the fill stops dead at the artwork.
`icon_cutout.py` does it.

**5. A dark stroke of 4 is a HEADING value.** Applied to 24px brown body text on
a cream panel it reads as mud. `textStroke` is explicit per label, and 0 is the
right answer for small dark text.

**6. THE PNG AND THE .model.json CAN AGREE ON EVERY VALUE AND STILL DISAGREE ON
ARRANGEMENT.** This is the one real limit of the "same tree" guarantee, and every
instance of it was found by a Studio render, never by the preview:

- Shadow and Face as SIBLINGS meant a `UIListLayout` gave each shadow its own
  cell - four tabs rendered as eight. Each element is now wrapped so the wrapper
  is the single layout item.
- The decorative `Highlight` frame inside a laid-out face claimed a slot and
  shoved price text out of its button. `UICorner`/`UIGradient`/`UIStroke` are not
  `GuiObject`s so layouts ignore them; only a Frame is caught.
- No `LayoutOrder` meant a grid came back in arbitrary order.
- `TextScaled` fills the whole label box while the renderer uses
  `height * textScale`, so Studio text ran large until a `UITextSizeConstraint`
  capped it.

- `TextScaled` **does not overflow, it SHRINKS** - without limit. So the symptom
  of text that does not fit is never text outside a frame, it is text that has
  quietly become unreadable. The renderer now shrinks to fit exactly as Roblox
  does, and `verify_ui`'s `text_fit` check measures how far each label had to
  shrink and fails below 55% of its designed size or 11pt on the worst device.
  It caught three on the first run, all descriptive text sized for a monitor.

**Render one page in Studio before trusting a set of them.**

**7. Never replace a directory inside a cloud-synced folder.**
`mv` plus `cp -r` made the sync client write conflict copies named
`<file>-<machine name>.png` holding the NEW images while the OLD files kept the
canonical names. 37 icons updated, 4
silently did not, and it surfaced only as two stale icons in a screenshot. Copy
file by file.

---

## Workflow

### 1. Icons

Every icon in this skill is generated or drawn by the skill itself (no third-party icon pack is needed). A page builds before any icon exists: an `icon` element with no matching PNG is skipped in the preview and carries a named placeholder in the emitted tree.

**Generate on Cloudflare, not on a GPU.** Measured on the same prompts:

| | Kaggle / SDXL | Cloudflare / FLUX.1-schnell |
|---|---|---|
| Per icon | 59s | **1.2s** |
| 33-icon set | ~40 min | **~40s** |
| Rejected by the checks | 12 of 38 | **0 of 33** |

The reason is hardware, not prompting. Kaggle hands out a Tesla P100 (sm_60,
2016) or a T4, with no way to choose, and **neither supports bf16** - which every
current model is built around. A 12B FLUX-class model dies with CUDA OOM on that
card even with CPU offload. Cloudflare runs it on their hardware and returns a
PNG.

    python scripts/gen_icons_cf.py --manifest <your icons manifest>.json         --out <project>/_cf_raw
    python scripts/icon_cutout.py --in <project>/_cf_raw --out <project>/icons         --size 256 --sheet <project>/icons_sheet.png
    python scripts/glyphs.py --out <project>/icons --size 256
    python scripts/upload_icons.py --icons <project>/icons --map <project>/icons.json

`references/icons.example.json` shows the manifest format (a shared `style`
anchor plus one short subject prompt per icon). Needs `CF_ACCOUNT_ID` and
`CF_API_TOKEN` (Account > Workers AI > Read). The
budget is **10,000 neurons/day**, and the MEASURED cost is **~141 neurons per
1024px 4-step image**, so about **70 images/day**. The published per-tile formula
predicts 57.6 and is 2.4x optimistic - trust the dashboard, not the price list.

Two operational facts: the endpoint takes **only `prompt` and `steps`** (width,
height and seed return HTTP 400, so there is **no seed** and a reroll is a real
reroll), and the safety filter throws false positives - "one metal grain silo
tower" came back NSFW, which needs a **reword, not a retry**.

Then **look at the sheet**. The check that matters is `extra_objects`: image
models pluralise small nouns, and a sheet of seven chickens passes every colour
statistic ever written. A multi-object generation is CROPPED to the best object
plus anything clustered with it, and flagged `SALVAGED` so it gets looked at.

**SYMBOLS ARE DRAWN, NOT GENERATED**, and that held for every model tried.
`glyphs.py` draws close, tick, heart, star, lock, plus, minus and arrow with a
dilation-based uniform outline. Generated attempts returned a scribble for the X,
a down-arrow for the tick and a games controller for the heart. Geometry is not
an image-generation problem, and a drawn set is consistent by construction.

Kaggle is OFF for everything, icons and meshes alike (see the notice at the top):
its terms ban this use. Use the Cloudflare route above.

### 2. Pages

Write a small spec generator (a Python script that builds the dicts with
`scripts/ui_kit.py`), not five hand-edited JSON files. A typical set is five
pages: HUD, shop, inventory, quests, settings.

```bash
python scripts/ui_build.py <your spec>.json --out mockups --icons icons
# builds all three outputs; pass --png / --model / --luau to build only some
```

Elements: `panel`, `button`, `frame`, `label`, `icon`. Containers take
`layout: {type: list|grid, ...}`, `padding` and `aspect`. Sizes and positions are
UDim2 `[sx, ox, sy, oy]` with an `anchor` - Roblox's rules, not CSS.

Every `panel` and `button` expands to **the depth stack** automatically: a shadow
offset down in a darker, hue-shifted-toward-blue colour, a face with a top-lit
`UIGradient` at rotation -90, and a dark outer `UIStroke` of identical thickness
everywhere. That stack is the whole difference between flat and professional in
both community guides, and it is not a per-element decision.

The guides' **inset bright highlight is OFF by default**. It reads as a lit
edge on a saturated Figma button and as a second border with a visible gap in
Roblox; on cream panels it looked like white lines drawn on everything. The
gradient already carries the top-light. Re-enable per element with
`highlight: true`, or theme-wide.

### 3. Into Studio

Paste `Page.lua` into `execute_luau`, then `capture_screenshot`. A `ScreenGui`
under `StarterGui` renders live in the viewport, so the UI is checkable in EDIT
mode with no playtest: the viewport renders a `ScreenGui` under `StarterGui` live,
so drive the real controller into it and screenshot. Clear the injected
instances afterwards so the saved place carries no drift.

Icons still need real asset IDs. `to_instances` emits
`rbxassetid://ICON_<NAME>` placeholders - upload with `roblox-3d-model`'s
`upload_asset.py` as **assetType Image, never Decal** (a Decal wraps an image and
has a different id; assigning it renders nothing, with no error), then
substitute.

---

### 4. Responsiveness

Pages are authored at a **reference resolution in offset** - which is how the
guides build, and what keeps a design predictable - and mapped to the player's
viewport by **one `UIScale` on the CanvasFrame**, driven by
`references/UIController.client.lua` from `ViewportSize`.

There is deliberately **no floor** on that scale. A floor of 0.60 was tried and
was the wrong lever: it made the page render at 768x432 on a 640x360 phone, so it
stopped FITTING, which is worse than being small.

Touch targets are protected at the source instead. 44pt on a 640x360 phone means
**88px at a 1280x720 reference**, so `ui_kit.TOUCH_H` is 88 and every interactive
control is sized from it. That is what "mobile first" actually costs, and it is
why the shop TILE is the button rather than a small pill inside it.

`verify_ui.py` evaluates every page at four real viewports (640x360, 896x414,
1024x768, 1920x1080), applies the scale, and fails anything under the minimum
with the exact px it needs. Run it before believing a page works anywhere but
your monitor.

---

## Layout hygiene: the three things a human notices in one second

These are the complaints a player makes about a UI that passed every other check
on this list, and they are now enforced by `verify_ui.py` rather than left to
taste. They are measured on the RESOLVED rectangles at the reference resolution,
not read off the property tree, because every one of them is a rendering fact.

**1. ELEMENTS MUST NEVER TOUCH.** Minimum 8px between siblings at the reference
resolution; an overlap is a failure, a gap under 8px is a warning. Two controls
with no space between them read as one control with a line through it, and at the
smallest supported scale a 1px gap is a 0px gap. Anything meant to sit on top of
something else - a sweep over a cooldown dial, a value over a bar - declares
itself with `"overhang": true`, so that "these overlap" always means either a bug
or a decision somebody wrote down. Checks: `sibling_overlap`, `sibling_gap`.

**2. CENTRED IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PROPERTY.** An element that asks to be
centred has its rendered centre compared against its parent's, to 1.5px. The
classic Roblox bug is a `0.5` scale position with no `0.5` anchor: the element
lands **half its own size** off centre, which looks almost right, and it is
exactly the error the checker names when it sees it. Never eyeball centring off a
mockup - the mockup is drawn from the same numbers that are wrong. Check:
`off_centre`.

**3. NO BOX DRAWN AROUND A CONTROL.** A frame that exists only to position
something must be `"transparent": true`. An opaque container hugging one child -
within 6px on every side - is not a container, it is an outline nobody asked for,
and it is the box-around-a-button defect. The same
applies to a bar's track hugging its fill. If a control needs a visible border,
that is a stroke or a padded panel with a stated padding, not an accidental
wrapper. Check: `wrapper_box`.

**A note on what these checks cost.** They fire on layouts that were signed off
by eye and by every other gate, which is the point - but a warning is not a
licence to widen every gap to 8px mechanically. Read what it names, then either
fix the spacing or declare the overlap. What is not acceptable is leaving it
unexamined because the page "looks fine" in the mockup at 1280x720.

## Iterate on `verify_ui.py`, not on the mockup

The mockup PNG is for a human and for sign-off. It is not the iteration loop:
an image is re-sent on every later tool call in the same context, so re-opening
it after each tweak is the most expensive way to ask a question the checker
already answers in text. `verify_ui.py` names the element, the number and the
rule it broke. **Fix against the text, then look at the PNG once, when the page
is done.**

This is not a licence to skip the look. The checker cannot see taste, colour
weight, or whether a screen reads at a glance - and it is drawn from the same
resolved tree as the layout, so it agrees with the layout by construction. One
honest look at the end, at the reference resolution.

## Non-negotiables

- **Scale, not Offset**, for size and position. The exception is
  `UIStroke.Thickness`, which genuinely has no scale.
- **Touch targets 44pt minimum.** Action buttons 70x70 on small screens.
- **Keep the thumbstick zone (bottom left), the jump zone (bottom right) and the
  36px top bar clear.** Put a hotbar bottom-CENTRE for exactly
  this reason.
- **One frame per page**, transparent, so a scripter toggles one `.Visible`.
- **`UIAspectRatioConstraint` inside grid cells**, or tiles distort.
- **Stroke thickness identical across the screen.** Mixed weights is the single
  clearest tell of beginner or generated UI.
- **Text must fit its box at a legible size**, checked by `text_fit`. Do not
  "solve" a long string by shrinking the label; widen the box or shorten the text.
- **Never hardcode a text colour.** Use `ink`, `inkSoft`, `onDark` from the theme.
  A test on a dark theme produced perfect layout with invisible item
  names because one component had a light-panel brown baked in.
- **Green price buttons, with the currency icon on them.** A convention, not a
  preference.
- **Nothing touches, everything that says it is centred is centred, and no frame
  draws a box round its child.** See "Layout hygiene" above - three checks, all
  enforced.

## Themes: writing your own theme file

A spec's `"theme"` is either an inline object or a path to a JSON file, resolved
relative to the spec. `references/theme.json` is the default and the template to
copy. Every value in it is read by the renderer and the emitter from the one
file, so changing it restyles the PNG and the `.model.json` together.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stroke` | Outer `UIStroke` thickness on panels and buttons (default theme: 5) |
| `textStroke` | Default text stroke (4); override per label, 0 for small dark text |
| `corner` | Corner radius as a scale (0.2) |
| `shadowOffset` | Pixels the depth-stack shadow sits below the face (7) |
| `outline` | Hex colour of every stroke |
| `backdrop` | Preview-only ground: one hex, or two hexes for a vertical gradient |
| `backdropImage` | Optional preview-only screenshot of your game world to judge the UI over; never emitted |
| `palette` | Named colours (`panel`, `gold`, `green`, `ink`, `onDark`, ...). Elements refer to them by name; never hardcode a text colour |
| `font`, `fontStyle` | `FredokaOne` (default, bundled), `BuilderSans`, `SourceSans`, `Merriweather`, `Montserrat`. Only Fredoka previews exactly; the others fall back to a system font in the PNG and Studio is truth |
| `flat` | `true` emits solid fills instead of the top-lit gradient |
| `highlight` | `true` turns the inset highlight on theme-wide |
| `motion` | Hover, press and open-style numbers, emitted as attributes and played by `references/UIController.client.lua` |

Panels take `alpha` for translucency.

**Surfaces carry a PATTERN layer, not just a gradient.** `scripts/patterns.py` draws
sheen, stripes, dots, clouds and grain; any panel/button/frame takes
`"pattern": {name, colour, opacity, tile, fade}`. Leaving it out is why a UI built
from shapes alone reads flat. Upload `pattern_*.png` with the icons. A patterned
surface moves its children into a `Content` frame so a layout never grabs the
pattern.

**Motion is data too.** A theme's `"motion"` block (hover scale/rotate/time/style,
press scale/time, page open style) is emitted as attributes and played by
`references/UIController.client.lua`. Many games open menus INSTANTLY and put the
motion on buttons and content. The PNG cannot prove motion - playtest it.

## `verify_labels.py` - the dead-label gate

```bash
python verify_labels.py --ui src/ui --client src/client
```

Every label carrying the placeholder sentinel must be named by some controller,
or the build fails. This is the gate for the placeholder rule at the top of this
file, and it is proven to fail: rename one binding and it goes red.

It understands two shapes of reference - the literal (`"AmmoCount"`) and one
ASSEMBLED from a row index (`` `BankRow{i}` .. "Name" ``), because a first
version understood only the literal and reported ten WORKING labels as dead.
`--sentinel` overrides the default `<unbound>`; whatever you choose, it must be a
string the live code can never produce.
